steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Stir in spaghetti and return to a boil. Cook until pasta is tender but still slightly firm, about 10 minutes. Drain well.
Transfer spaghetti to a large bowl and toss with spaghetti sauce until well combined.
Mix cottage cheese and sour cream in a bowl.
Spread half the spaghetti with sauce into the prepared baking dish.
Spread the cottage cheese mixture evenly over the spaghetti.
Place the remaining spaghetti and sauce in an even layer over the cottage cheese mixture; sprinkle with mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and the cheese is browned, 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Leftover Spaghetti Lasagna
raw_recipe.description: Get the flavor of lasagna with the easiest layered baked spaghetti dish ever. Just mix cooked thin spaghetti with prepared sauce, layer with cottage cheese, sprinkle with mozzarella cheese, and bake. It's a perfect way to use up left-over spaghetti.

review.reviewBody: I made a homemade meat marinara to go in this casserole. Instead of fat free sour cream, I used reduced fat. The family thought this was great--they ate every bite. NO LEFTOVERS. This was perfect for me because I could make the marinara in the crockpot and quick make the pasta, then mix and bake. I'll make this again.

To make this, I had to cook more spaghetti noodles, as all I had leftover were homemade Italian-American meatballs -- crumbled into pieces -- and homemade marinara sauce. Also, I had no cottage cheese, so just mixed regular sour cream with a little shredded Parmesan, and added the end of a package of Cheddar to the mozzarella. It baked covered for 30 minutes, and uncovered for 10. Delicious!

We put 5 sweet Italian sausages on bottom of 11x7 glass pan and baked at 400 degrees while preparing everything else. Then put 2 cups of sauce mixed in spaghetti. Put half over sausages, 1 cup ricotta spread over the spaghetti and then the remainder of the spaghetti. Put 6 oz of mozzarella on top and baked 25". Very good, Thank you!

Really enjoyable. I did put some cooked meat on the bottom - a mixture we can buy at the grocery store that has hamburger, ground pork and ground veal. And I added some Italian sausage meat as well. Cooked it up with onions and mushrooms. Layered that onto the bottom of the pan, then some wilted spinach, then half of the pasta and sauce. Topped that with the cottage cheese and sour cream mix. Finally topped it with the rest of the pasta and sauce and then the cheese. I didn't find it took as long to cook so I would recommend watching it so the cheese doesn't overcook. Will definitely make it again....with my modifications.

Three stars for a good idea that is faultily executed. I didn't make it as is because... Cottage cheese? I used a ricotta, egg, Romano and parsley mixture that is no trouble to mix up and a lot better. I also used a meat marinara sauce. But I like the idea which I hadn't seen before so I give kudos for that. I also put a thin layer of sauce in the bottom of the pan and on the top before the cheese exactly as though I were making a real lasagna.

Followed ingredients exactly. I used leftover spaghetti. I added a little extra sauce (from a jar) because the leftover spaghetti seemed too dry. This made the final product a little too wet. I didn't take into account that the sour cream & cottage cheese would add additional liquid. I kept the dish loosely covered with foil for half the baking time because I don't like for the cheese to get overly browned too quickly. I uncovered it for the last 20 min. Everyone loved this dish and had seconds. Although we all loved it... I feel like it needs a little more seasoning. Next time I think I will mix in some Italian seasoning, salt and pepper into the cottage cheese mixture. Great way to use leftover spaghetti. I think I will start making extra spaghetti ON PURPOSE and put in freezer so I can make this dish the following week.

First of all, to the person who gave it one star and said "no true lasagna recipe would use cottage cheese and sour cream"... I don't recall this recipe saying it was was authentic anything?? This is a recipe utilizing leftovers. It is what it is, and it is wonderful.

Yes having married into an Italian family I wondered about the filling too. And all I have to say is I LOVE IT and will probably swap it for the typical bland ricotta I usually use in my Italian cooking. I added a little parmesan and some Italian seasoning to it. It was WONDERFUL!

I keep my own homemade sauce in the freezer in great proportions so I used that. I did follow the "tip" and put Italian sausage on the bottom prior to layering.

Regardless, I love this concept and i LOVE LOVE the cottage cheese/sour cream filling! 

Thank you for posting this recipe! I will most definitely prepare it again and again!

I didn't use sour cream & cottage cheese. I went with the traditional ricotta & parm, but I did ADD some things, since my leftover spaghetti fell short of more than one layer. I made more tomato based sauce with kale for a healthy kick, topping it off with 5 Italian Cheese blend instead of just mozzarella. OMG, it was so tasty, & still is bcuz I now have Spaghetti Lasagna leftovers that I had to freeze. It still tastes the same even after being frozen.

My grandma made something like this growing up - it combines the yumminess of lasagna and spaghetti. 
What is this fat free sour cream? Bleck. In place of that abomination and cottage cheese (ew) I added whole milk ricotta mixed with two eggs. I also added browned hamburger to the sauce, which I doubled. 
Super nummy and sure to please even picky eaters.

My husband and I LOVED this recipe! I love spaghetti but my husband thinks it's boring so I never make it. When I found this recipe I was so excited to try it! I did add egg to the cheese mixture as others had mentioned and also added Italian seasonings and garlic. We both went back for seconds ?
It's not really left over spaghetti if you prepare it as your making this dish. I have been making this for years using left-over spaghetti....it's much much better.
I found my choices and just loves it. We look forward to it.
I have always made my lasagna with spaghetti. I don’t like the lasagna noodles because they are too chewy. I don’t use sour cream only cottage cheese and mozzarella. Love my recipe.
I used pepperonis
I don't like sour cream, I used ricotta cheese instead. That's the only thing I changed. My family loved it!!

This isn't a favorite for my 3 young children but they do eat it. I like it because it is an easy way to use leftover pasta. I have made the recipe as is and they never knew it was cottage cheese. I have also used ricotta because I had it on hand and we all liked the texture of the ricotta compared to the cottage cheese. Our new recipe to re- purpose leftover pasta, many thanks for sharing.
I loved it! Easy and economical to boot.
I really wanted to like this, but the flavor mix with the sour cream just didn't sit well with me. my husband liked it though. That's what counts!

We made this last night with our leftover spaghetti and meatballs, but still layered with the cottage cheese and sour cream. The only thing we did different was we added a layer of Spinach. Absolutely delicious! This is definitely one of the best casserole dishes we’ve ever made. Such amazing comfort food especially during quarantine. Thank you for a great recipe!
I used left over spaghetti and added parm to the layers. We absolutely loved it!
